events.title: Early Settlement and Trade
events.description: Early settlements emerged in Jordan region, located on important trade routes. The area connected Mesopotamia, Egypt and Mediterranean, caravans transported spices, frankincense and other precious goods. Jordan's strategic position made it crossroads of ancient world.

events.title: Iron Age Kingdoms
events.description: Iron Age kingdoms like Ammon, Moab and Edom emerged in Jordan region. These Semitic kingdoms mentioned frequently in Bible, interacting frequently with Israel Kingdom. Edomites in Petra area controlled southern trade routes.

events.title: Rise of the Nabataeans
events.description: Arab Nabataeans established a kingdom in southern Jordan with Petra as capital. Nabataeans controlled frankincense trade routes, accumulating enormous wealth. They carved magnificent structures in rose-red rock, developing advanced water management systems.

events.title: Petra Golden Age
events.description: Nabataean Kingdom reached zenith, Petra became wealthy trade center with 20,000 population. Nabataeans built complex canals and cisterns in desert, making city prosper. The Treasury (Al-Khazneh) is Petra's most famous structure.

events.title: Roman Annexation of Nabataea
events.description: Roman Emperor Trajan annexed Nabataean Kingdom, establishing Arabia province with capital Bostra (southern Syria today). Petra continued prospering, but as maritime trade developed, overland trade declined, city gradually declined.

events.title: Great Earthquake
events.description: Major earthquake destroyed much of Petra's architecture, accelerating city's decline. Though partially rebuilt, Petra never recovered former glory. City gradually abandoned, disappeared into history, until 'rediscovered' by Western explorers in 19th century.

events.title: Christianity Spreads
events.description: Jordan became part of Byzantine Empire, Christianity flourished. Madaba famous for exquisite Byzantine mosaics, including famous 6th century Holy Land map. Many churches and monasteries built during this period.

events.title: Battle of Mu'tah
events.description: First major conflict between Muslims and Byzantines occurred at Mu'tah in Jordan. Though Muslims repelled, battle demonstrated their military potential. Prophet Muhammad's adopted son Zayd fell here.

events.title: Incorporation into Islam after Yarmouk
events.description: After Battle of Yarmouk, Jordan became part of Islamic Caliphate. Region gradually Islamized and Arabized. Umayyad caliphs built desert castles in Jordan, serving as hunting lodges and caravan stations.

events.title: Umayyad Desert Castles
events.description: Umayyad caliphs built luxurious castles in Jordan desert, such as Qusayr 'Amra and Qasr al-Kharana. These structures blended Byzantine, Persian and Islamic styles, decorated with exquisite frescoes and mosaics.

events.title: Crusader Occupation
events.description: Crusaders established strongholds in Jordan, including Kerak and Montreal castles. These fortresses controlled pilgrimage and trade routes, threatening Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca. Reynald of Kerak notorious for raiding caravans and brutality.

events.title: Saladin Recaptures Jordan
events.description: Saladin conquered Crusader castles in Jordan after Battle of Hattin. Jordan returned to Muslim rule, successively part of Ayyubid, Mamluk and Ottoman empires.

events.title: Ottoman Rule Begins
events.description: Ottoman Empire conquered Jordan, ruling for 400 years. Jordan became part of Damascus province. Under Ottoman rule, Jordan relatively peaceful but marginalized, economy declined, population decreased, Bedouin tribes nomadic in desert.

events.title: Petra 'Rediscovered'
events.description: Swiss explorer Burckhardt disguised as Muslim pilgrim, became first European to describe Petra to West. Petra's 'rediscovery' aroused great European interest, becoming archaeological and tourist hotspot.

events.title: Arab Revolt
events.description: Sharif Hussein of Mecca launched Arab Revolt against Ottoman rule. His sons Faisal and Abdullah led armies, fighting with assistance of British officer Lawrence. Jordan was important battlefield of revolt.

events.title: Battle of Aqaba
events.description: Faisal and Lawrence led Arab army attacking from desert, surprisingly capturing Aqaba port. This victory opened road to Syria, became turning point of Arab Revolt, also famous from film 'Lawrence of Arabia.'

events.title: Sykes-Picot Agreement and Partition
events.description: After war, Britain and France divided Middle East according to secret agreement, betraying promises to Arabs. Faisal's Syrian Kingdom overthrown by France. Transjordan region assigned to British mandate Palestine.

events.title: Establishment of Transjordan Emirate
events.description: After Cairo Conference, Britain installed Hussein's second son Abdullah as Emir of Transjordan. Abdullah originally planned to march to Syria to avenge brother, but accepted Transjordan rule. Britain retained actual control, but gave Abdullah considerable autonomy.

events.title: Anglo-Transjordan Treaty
events.description: Britain signed treaty with Transjordan, recognizing Abdullah as Emir, but Britain retained control of defense and foreign affairs. Treaty established protectorate status, Abdullah worked to gradually gain more autonomy.

events.title: Jordanian Independence
events.description: The Emirate of Transjordan gained independence, renamed the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan. Abdullah elevated from Emir to King. May 25 became Independence Day. Though independent, Jordan remained heavily dependent on British military and financial aid.

events.title: Assassination of King Abdullah
events.description: King Abdullah was assassinated by a Palestinian radical at Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem for alleged secret negotiations with Israel. His grandson Hussein was beside him, a bullet struck Hussein's chest medal, saving his life. This traumatic event profoundly affected young Hussein.

events.title: First Arab-Israeli War and West Bank
events.description: Jordan participated in Arab coalition attacking Israel. Jordanian Arab Legion under British officer Glubb performed best, occupying Jerusalem Old City and West Bank. Jordan's territory doubled, but massive Palestinian refugees flooded in, changing country's demographic composition.

events.title: Annexation of West Bank
events.description: King Abdullah formally annexed West Bank, incorporating it into Jordan. This unilateral action not recognized by other Arab states. Jordan became only Arab country granting Palestinians citizenship.

events.title: Hussein Ascends Throne
events.description: Abdullah's son Talal abdicated due to mental illness, 16-year-old Hussein became King. After official coronation in 1953, Hussein ruled Jordan for nearly half a century, becoming one of the Middle East's longest-serving and most respected leaders.

events.title: Dismissal of General Glubb
events.description: Hussein dismissed British General Glubb, ending British command of Jordanian military. This bold move enhanced Hussein's nationalist reputation, marking Jordan's break from British control.

events.title: Six-Day War and Loss of West Bank
events.description: Jordan joined Egypt and Syria against Israel but was quickly defeated. Israel occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem. Jordan lost its most prosperous region and holy sites, 300,000 refugees fled to the East Bank. This was one of Jordan's greatest disasters.

events.title: Battle of Karameh
events.description: Israel raided PLO bases in Jordan, Jordanian army and PLO jointly resisted. Though casualties heavy, this battle propagandized as Arab victory, boosting PLO and Arafat's prestige.

events.title: Black September
events.description: PLO armed groups grew increasingly powerful in Jordan, challenging royal authority. After PFLP hijacked planes to Jordan, Hussein ordered the military to suppress the PLO. Bloody civil war lasted 10 months, thousands died, PLO was expelled to Lebanon. This event was called 'Black September.'

events.title: Yom Kippur War
events.description: Jordan sent armored brigade to Syrian front, but avoided full involvement in war. Hussein more cautious after 1967 debacle, trying to balance Arab solidarity with protecting kingdom.

events.title: Rabat Summit Resolution
events.description: Arab League recognized PLO as sole legitimate representative of Palestinians. Jordan forced to relinquish sovereignty claims over West Bank. Hussein accepted resolution, but Jordan continued maintaining ties with West Bank.

events.title: Severing Legal Ties with West Bank
events.description: Facing Palestinian Intifada and PLO pressure, Hussein announced severing Jordan's administrative and legal ties with West Bank. This decision clearly indicated West Bank was Palestinian territory, paving way for later peace process.

events.title: Parliamentary Elections and Political Liberalization
events.description: After economic crisis and riots, Hussein restored parliamentary elections, opening political liberalization process. Islamic Action Front won majority seats. Hussein allowed certain degree of democracy while maintaining stability.

events.title: Gulf War Crisis
events.description: After Iraq invaded Kuwait, Jordan in awkward position. Hussein due to economic dependence and popular pressure didn't join anti-Iraq coalition, seen as supporting Saddam. This damaged Jordan's relations with US and Gulf states, leading to sanctions and aid cuts.

events.title: Peace Treaty with Israel
events.description: King Hussein and Israeli PM Rabin signed a peace treaty at the Arava border, ending 46 years of war. Jordan became the second Arab country to sign peace with Israel (after Egypt). The treaty resolved borders, water resources, and refugee issues, restoring Jordan's relations with the West.

events.title: Israeli Soldier Shooting Incident
events.description: Jordanian soldier shot seven Israeli schoolgirls at border. Israeli PM Netanyahu demanded severe punishment, but Hussein personally went to Israel, knelt before victims' families to apologize. This humanitarian gesture won Israelis' respect and emotion.

events.title: Death of King Hussein
events.description: King Hussein died after battling cancer, aged 63, having ruled Jordan for 46 years. Global leaders attended the funeral, including four US presidents. Hussein was known for wisdom, courage, and humanitarianism, keeping Jordan stable in a turbulent Middle East.

events.title: Abdullah II Ascends
events.description: Hussein changed succession before death, designating eldest son Abdullah as Crown Prince. 37-year-old Abdullah II inherited the throne. Educated in Britain and US, he served in the military. Abdullah promised to continue his father's legacy and reforms.

events.title: Counterterrorism Cooperation with US
events.description: After 9/11, Jordan became important US ally in Middle East war on terror. Jordanian intelligence closely cooperated with US, providing intelligence and training. This strengthened US-Jordan relations, but also made Jordan target of extremists.

events.title: Iraq War Impact
events.description: US invasion of Iraq brought Jordan challenges and opportunities. Jordan didn't participate in war but allowed US military use of its airspace and facilities. Hundreds of thousands of Iraqi refugees flooded into Jordan. Meanwhile, Iraq became market for Jordanian goods.

events.title: Amman Hotel Bombings
events.description: Al-Qaeda in Iraq launched suicide bombings at three Amman hotels, 60 dead, including Jordanian intelligence officers. Attacks shocked Jordan, triggering massive anti-terror demonstrations. Jordan strengthened security measures, combating extremism.

events.title: Arab Spring Protests
events.description: Inspired by Arab Spring, Jordan erupted in protests demanding political reform. But protests smaller scale, main demands were reform not overthrowing monarchy. Abdullah dismissed government, promised reforms, including amending constitution and election law.

events.title: Syrian Refugee Crisis
events.description: After Syrian Civil War erupted, over 1.3 million Syrian refugees fled to Jordan (including unregistered). With Jordan's population only 10 million, refugee influx severely burdened economy, infrastructure and social services. Jordan established camps like Zaatari and Azraq, receiving international aid.

events.title: Fighting ISIS
events.description: Jordan joined US-led coalition against ISIS, Jordanian warplanes bombed ISIS targets. This made Jordan enemy of ISIS, but Jordan firmly combated terrorism.

events.title: Lieutenant Kasasbeh Burned Alive
events.description: Jordanian pilot Lieutenant Kasasbeh captured by ISIS then burned alive, video released online. This brutal act enraged Jordan, King Abdullah cut short US visit to return home, vowed revenge. Jordan intensified airstrikes against ISIS.

events.title: Karak Attack
events.description: ISIS supporters attacked tourist city Karak, killing 10 including tourists and security personnel. Attack hit Jordan's important tourism industry. Government strengthened security, vowed to eliminate terrorism.

events.title: Economic Protests
events.description: Government subsidy cuts and tax increases triggered massive protests. People protested high prices, unemployment and corruption. Abdullah dismissed PM, new government withdrew some measures. But economic difficulties persisted, Jordan's debt high.

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.description: COVID pandemic devastated Jordan's economy, especially tourism. Government implemented strict lockdowns, but economic losses severe. Unemployment soared, especially among youth and women. Pandemic exacerbated Jordan's economic vulnerability.

events.title: Royal Crisis
events.description: Prince Hamzah (King's half-brother) accused of participating in destabilizing plot. Hamzah placed under house arrest, several senior officials arrested. Crisis eventually calmed, Hamzah signed loyalty pledge. This was rare public royal conflict in Jordan.

events.title: Ongoing Challenges
events.description: Jordan continues facing multiple challenges: economic difficulties, high unemployment (especially youth), water scarcity, refugee burden, regional instability. Jordan relies on foreign aid, especially from the US. But Jordan maintains relative stability, Abdullah continues balancing pressures, maintaining national security. Tourism to Petra slowly recovering.
